PullRequest.Title: Recognize eagerness option in PatchBased02Unified
PullRequest.Body: Recognize the `eagernessPrompt` option when it's provided with prompting strategy `PatchBased02Unified`

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The newly introduced unified strategy was not classified as an eagerness-aware prompt, so every qualifying inline-edit request redundantly installed an artificial post-response latency gate before yielding the first edit.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Users selecting explicit Medium or Low eagerness with PatchBased02Unified could wait until 700 ms or 1500 ms total request time before the first edit was displayed even when the model response was ready sooner.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Adding PatchBased02Unified to isEagernessPrompt recognizes that the model already receives eagerness through its prompt and skips the redundant client timing override, removing up to 700 ms (Medium) or 1500 ms (Low) from first-edit presentation without changing prompt construction or network request cardinality.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Commit ee9c82e739d0b52261d9804317f83d14f71429aa introduced PatchBased02Unified, but the base isEagernessPrompt whitelist omitted it. Model configuration preserves eagernessPrompt in overrideModelConfig, promptCrafting already emits the aggression tag for PatchBased02Unified, and _configureDebounceTimings calls _applyAggressivenessSettings whenever isEagernessPrompt is false. For explicit Medium/Low settings that path sets DelaySession.expectedTotalTime to the 700/1500 ms defaults, and stream parsing awaits the remaining artificial delay before yielding the first edit.

Scenarios.Scenario: A developer types and requests a next edit while the selected model uses PatchBased02Unified with eagernessPrompt='aggressionHighLow', especially with explicit Medium or Low eagerness.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model configuration is resolved, _configureDebounceTimings classifies the prompt, context and prompt construction complete, endpoint.makeChatRequest2 streams the response, response parsing computes edits, and the first edit is yielded. Before the diff, explicit Medium/Low installed a 700/1500 ms expected-total-time gate and the first parsed edit awaited its remainder; after the diff that redundant gate is skipped. Context gathering and the network response remain on the critical path; the removed wait was after response parsing began.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Streams one model response through endpoint.makeChatRequest2 for the primary request, with sequential fallback/cursor-jump requests only when their existing conditions trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One primary network call per uncached provider invocation; an existing sequential fallback may add one call on model NotFound, and an existing cursor-jump path may add a request after NoSuggestions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model request and retry structure ran before the diff; qualifying Medium/Low responses could then wait for the configured expected-total-time threshold before first yield.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The primary response must stream before an edit can be yielded. The diff only removes a client-side post-response wait and does not add, move, or multiply this call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally obtains language context and neighbor-file snippets before prompt construction when their existing model options enable them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one language-context gather and one neighbor-snippet gather per provider invocation; defaults shown in PromptOptions disable both, and no changed line alters those options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical optional context gathering occurred before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enabled context work completes or times out before the model request. Its placement and cardinality are unchanged by the predicate update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The behavior occurs per uncached inline-edit invocation using this strategy and option. Cost removed per qualifying request is bounded by the explicit eagerness setting's expected-total-time default (700 ms Medium, 1500 ms Low); request and boundary cardinality do not scale differently after the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each provider invocation starts one primary streaming request. Fallback after NotFound and cursor-jump retry after NoSuggestions are sequential generator paths, not parallel fan-out. The changed predicate neither starts requests nor changes cancellation, retry, or concurrency; because PatchBased02Unified already bakes debounce=0, removing the post-response artificial delay does not advance network dispatch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, cache population, coalescing, or invalidation code changes. PatchBased02Unified's baked cacheDelay=200 and rebasedCacheDelay=0 remain unchanged; the predicate affects the model-provider stream's first-yield delay, not warm-cache lookup behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed enum member makes isEagernessPrompt true; its only production caller then skips _applyAggressivenessSettings, which otherwise sets the 700/1500 ms expected total time, and the stream explicitly awaits the remaining artificial delay before first yield.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository establishes the exact configured upper bounds and call path, but not the prevalence of explicit Medium/Low settings or how often model responses arrive before those thresholds. This uncertainty affects aggregate impact, not the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes a redundant latency gate for an eagerness-aware model without adding work, boundary calls, retained state, or concurrency. The concrete pre-existing regression fix was recorded separately with its blamed introducing commit.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files and full diff pages. Traced the sole runtime consumer through inline-edit scheduling, optional context gathering, model network streaming, retries, and first-edit yield; checked cache and concurrency effects. Submitted no findings because the PR reduces latency and introduces no performance regression; recorded the verified regression fix for internal learning.
